handbookNote: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual, titled 'NATIONAL CDL MANUAL (Commercial Driver's License), With Supplement for Modernized Version' -- the AAMVA-authored '2005 Testing System (2017 Version) with Supplemental Sections 11 and 12,' Copyright 2005 AAMVA, Hy-Brid Version October 2023, with individual sections carrying their own 'Version: July 2017' or 'Version: March 2025' footers (final page footer 'MM1169 08/11/2026') -- published by the Iowa Department of Transportation and fetched directly from the official PDF at iowadot.gov/media/326/download (also mirrored at ia.iowadot.gov/pubs/CDL-manual.pdf) on 2026-08-22 (full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/ia_cdl_research/ia_cdl_manual.txt, 9,983 lines) -- price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Real exam mechanics: unlike the generic AAMVA manual text itself (which contains no state-specific question-count table), Iowa's own official CDL Testing page (iowadot.gov/drivers-licenses-ids/commercial-drivers/get-cdl/cdl-testing) states an explicit 'Types of CDL knowledge tests (number of questions/allowed to miss)' table, confirmed directly from the live page's raw HTML (not a third-party estimate): General knowledge for any CDL 50/10 (40 correct to pass); Combination vehicle for Class A 20/04 (16 correct); Air brake 25/05 (20 correct); Passenger 20/04 (16 correct); School bus 20/04 (16 correct); Doubles/Triples 20/04 (16 correct); Hazmat 30/06 (24 correct); Tank 20/04 (16 correct); Iowa operator (if applicable) 25/5 (20 correct) -- every test computes to exactly the federally standardized 80% minimum passing score under 49 CFR 383.135(a). This CDL-specific table is a separate, distinctly-confirmed official source from the general Iowa driver's-license practice-test page that this project's earlier ia_driver track build found could NOT be used to confirm a real-test question count (that page only describes a 25-question ONLINE PRACTICE test, explicitly distinct from the real exam); the CDL Testing page above instead directly labels these as the real CDL knowledge tests administered at DOT/County Treasurer locations by appointment, so its counts are asserted here with confidence. The four-step CDL process (pass knowledge tests, obtain a CLP, complete ELDT, pass the skills/drive test), minimum age 18 (21 for interstate commerce), and CLP/fee details ($12 CLP valid 1 year; CDL Class A/B/C $8/year issued for 8 years; endorsement fees: doubles/triples $5, tank $5, hazmat $5, passenger $10, school bus $10, combined hazmat/tank (X) $10 requiring both exams plus a TSA fingerprint-based threat assessment; restriction removal $10) were confirmed directly from iowadot.gov/drivers-licenses-ids/commercial-drivers/get-cdl, .../commercial-learner-permits-clp, and .../get-or-renew-drivers-licenses-ids-permits/fees. Content-depth rationale: this is the same generic AAMVA 2005 Testing System model manual used as a base by several other states already built in this project (comparable to Idaho's newer 2022 AAMVA edition), but Iowa has grafted in its own state-specific testing procedures via Supplemental Sections 11 (Vehicle Inspection Test, Version March 2025) and 12 (Basic Control Skills Test, Version March 2025) -- notably a distinctive Iowa-specific rule that the service brake check step of the pre-trip inspection is 'Verbally describe only, no physical demonstration will be required in Iowa,' plus detailed Iowa-specific scoring rules for pull-ups/encroachments/looks on the Basic Control Skills exercises and precise On-Road Driving test procedures (Section 13). It covers Section 1 Introduction (CMV/CDL definitions, Class A/B/C, six endorsements P/S/N/T/H/X, ten restriction codes, CLP rules, medical certification, disqualifications, ELDT), Section 2 Driving Safely (vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing, communicating, speed/space management, hazard perception, distracted driving, aggressive drivers, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, mountain driving, emergencies, ABS, skids, accidents, fires, alcohol/drugs, hazmat-for-all-drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely, Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely, Section 5 Air Brakes, Section 6 Combination Vehicles, Section 7 Doubles and Triples, Section 8 Tank Vehicles, Section 9 Hazardous Materials (intent of regulations, shipper/carrier/driver roles, communication rules/shipping papers/placarding, loading/unloading, driving/parking/emergency rules, glossary), Section 10 School Buses (danger zones/mirrors, loading/unloading, emergency evacuation, railroad crossings, student management, ABS, special safety considerations), Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test, Section 12 Basic Control Skills Test, and Section 13 On-Road Driving -- supporting a large, non-repetitive, well-grounded question pool of 577 raw questions before dedup. Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Iowa manual text or a specifically-cited iowadot.gov page, cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's numbers.
